en: Yesterday I missed the bus, so I walked to the office.
tamil: நேத்து பஸ்ஸை விட்டுட்டேன், அதனால ஆபீஸ் வரைக்கும் நடந்தே போனேன்.
context: Explaining to a colleague why you looked tired.
explain: 'Missed' and 'walked' are past tense. 'So' joins a result to its reason.
usage: Use it with colleagues to explain a small problem from the day before.
leelaQ: What happened to you on the way to work yesterday?
answer: Yesterday I missed the bus, so I took an auto.

en: What happened to you yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து உனக்கு என்ன ஆச்சு?
context: Asking a colleague why they were absent.
explain: 'What happened?' asks about an event. Use it to show concern.
usage: Use it with a colleague or friend who missed something.
leelaQ: Why did you miss the office or class last time?
answer: I missed it because I had a fever.

en: We went to Ooty last summer and it rained every day.
tamil: போன கோடையில ஊட்டிக்கு போனோம், தினமும் மழை பெய்துச்சு.
context: Telling a friend about a holiday.
explain: 'Went' is the past of 'go'. 'Last summer' tells when it happened.
usage: Use it when you share a trip story with friends or relatives.
leelaQ: Where did you go for your last holiday?
answer: We went to Munnar last year and the weather was lovely.

en: Please tell me what happened at the bank.
tamil: பேங்க்ல என்ன நடந்துச்சுன்னு தயவு செய்து சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a family member for the full story.
explain: 'Please tell me' is a polite request. 'What happened' follows without a question form.
usage: Use it with family or friends when you want the whole story.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about a time you went to a bank?
answer: I went to open an account and waited for an hour.

en: When I was small, I used to catch fish in the village pond.
tamil: நான் சின்னவனா இருந்தப்போ ஊர் குளத்துல மீன் பிடிப்பேன்.
context: Sharing a childhood memory with friends.
explain: 'Used to' talks about a habit in the past that does not happen now.
usage: Use it to talk about childhood with friends, cousins or new colleagues.
leelaQ: What did you love doing when you were a child?
answer: I used to play cricket in the street every evening.

en: I did not sleep well last night because of the noise.
tamil: சத்தம் காரணமா நேத்து ராத்திரி நல்லா தூங்கல.
context: Telling a colleague why you look tired.
explain: Negative past: 'did not' plus the base verb 'sleep'.
usage: Use it to explain tiredness to a friend or manager.
leelaQ: How did you sleep last night?
answer: I slept well because the night was cool.

en: I have visited Madurai three times this year.
tamil: இந்த வருஷம் மூணு தடவை மதுரைக்கு போயிருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend how often you travelled.
explain: Present perfect (have + visited) links past visits with now. 'This year' is not finished yet.
usage: Use it to say how many times you did something up to now.
leelaQ: How many times have you travelled this year?
answer: I have travelled four times this year, mostly for work.

en: Where did you go last weekend?
tamil: போன வார இறுதியில எங்க போனீங்க?
context: Starting a Monday chat with a friend.
explain: Use 'did' plus the base verb 'go' in past questions. Do not say 'did you went'.
usage: Use it on Monday to start a friendly talk at work or college.
leelaQ: What did you do on the last weekend?
answer: I went to my native place with my family.

en: First I called the mechanic, then I waited near the bike for an hour.
tamil: முதல்ல மெக்கானிக்கை கூப்பிட்டேன், அப்புறம் வண்டி பக்கத்துலயே ஒரு மணி நேரம் காத்திருந்தேன்.
context: Describing what happened when your bike broke down.
explain: 'First' and 'then' show the order of events in a story.
usage: Use it to tell events in order when you explain a problem to a friend.
leelaQ: What did you do when your vehicle broke down?
answer: First I stopped on the side, then I called my brother.

en: Did you enjoy the trip to Kodaikanal?
tamil: கொடைக்கானல் டிரிப் ரசிச்சீங்களா?
context: Asking a friend after their holiday.
explain: Past yes/no questions start with 'Did' and use the base verb.
usage: Use it when a friend or colleague comes back from a trip.
leelaQ: Did you enjoy your last trip, and why?
answer: Yes, I enjoyed it because the weather was cool.

en: My phone fell into the water, and I panicked.
tamil: என் ஃபோன் தண்ணில விழுந்துடுச்சு, நான் பயந்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a small accident.
explain: 'Fell' is the irregular past of 'fall'. 'Panicked' shows a sudden fear.
usage: Use it to share a stressful moment in a casual chat.
leelaQ: Have you ever dropped your phone? What happened?
answer: Yes, I dropped it in the bucket and it stopped working.

en: Could you tell me how the interview went?
tamil: இன்டர்வியூ எப்படி போச்சுன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend after a job interview.
explain: 'Could you' is polite. 'How the interview went' stays in statement order.
usage: Use it to politely ask about someone's recent experience.
leelaQ: How did your last interview or exam go?
answer: It went well, and I answered most questions.

en: After we finished lunch, we all went to see a movie.
tamil: சாப்பிட்டு முடிச்சப்புறம் எல்லாரும் சினிமாவுக்கு போனோம்.
context: Telling a colleague about a family outing.
explain: 'After' joins two past events. The first event happened before the second.
usage: Use it to tell what you did after a meal or event.
leelaQ: What did you do last Sunday after lunch?
answer: After lunch we rested for some time and then visited my aunt.

en: We have not met each other since college.
tamil: காலேஜுக்கு அப்புறம் நாங்க ஒருத்தரை ஒருத்தர் பார்க்கவே இல்ல.
context: Talking about an old friend.
explain: 'Have not' with 'since' shows a long time without an action.
usage: Use it when you talk about an old friend you have lost touch with.
leelaQ: Who is an old friend you haven't met for years?
answer: I have not met my school friend Ravi for ten years.

en: I have just come back from my cousin's wedding.
tamil: நான் இப்பதான் என் மாமா பையன் கல்யாணத்துல இருந்து வந்தேன்.
context: Telling a neighbour where you were.
explain: 'Have just' means something finished a very short time ago.
usage: Use it when someone asks where you were, or why you are tired.
leelaQ: Have you been to a wedding recently?
answer: Yes, I have just attended my friend's wedding in Salem.

en: Have you ever been to Rameswaram?
tamil: நீங்க எப்பவாவது ராமேஸ்வரம் போயிருக்கீங்களா?
context: Asking about someone's travel experience.
explain: 'Have you ever...?' asks about experience in a whole life.
usage: Use it to ask new friends about places they have visited.
leelaQ: Have you ever been to a famous temple town?
answer: Yes, I have been to Madurai and Tirupati.

en: Last month my brother lost his wallet in the train.
tamil: போன மாசம் என் தம்பி ரயில்ல பர்ஸை தொலைச்சுட்டான்.
context: Telling a friend about a family problem.
explain: 'Lost' is the past of 'lose'. 'Last month' tells us when.
usage: Use it to tell a friend a sad or unlucky event from the past.
leelaQ: Did you ever lose something important?
answer: Yes, I once lost my ID card in the market.

en: What did you do after the exam finished?
tamil: பரீட்சை முடிஞ்சப்புறம் என்ன பண்ணுனீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about the day of the exam.
explain: 'What did you do' asks about an action. 'After' adds the time order.
usage: Use it to ask what someone did after an event.
leelaQ: What did you do after your last exam?
answer: I went home and slept for a few hours.

en: I was cooking when the gas cylinder ran out.
tamil: நான் சமைச்சுட்டு இருந்தப்போ கேஸ் சிலிண்டர் தீர்ந்துடுச்சு.
context: Telling a neighbour about a kitchen problem.
explain: Past continuous (was cooking) shows the long action. Simple past (ran out) shows the sudden one.
usage: Use it to explain what you were doing when something suddenly happened.
leelaQ: What were you doing when the power went off?
answer: I was watching TV when the power went off.

en: Tell me about your last holiday.
tamil: உங்க கடைசி விடுமுறையை பத்தி சொல்லுங்க.
context: Chatting with a new friend.
explain: A simple imperative to invite someone to tell their story.
usage: Use it in casual chats to start a story.
leelaQ: Where did you spend your last holiday?
answer: I went to Pondicherry and enjoyed the beach.

en: Finally, the auto driver found the right street after one hour.
tamil: கடைசியா ஆட்டோ டிரைவர் ஒரு மணி நேரம் கழிச்சு சரியான தெருவை கண்டுபிடிச்சார்.
context: Telling a friend about a long journey.
explain: 'Finally' shows the last event in a story after some waiting.
usage: Use it at the end of a story to show the problem was solved.
leelaQ: Have you ever got lost in a new place?
answer: Yes, I got lost in Bangalore and a shopkeeper showed me the way.

en: He never told me about the accident.
tamil: அவன் விபத்தை பத்தி எனக்கு எப்பவுமே சொல்லல.
context: Complaining that a friend hid something.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. It is used with a past verb.
usage: Use it when someone did not share important news with you.
leelaQ: Do you like to share bad news with friends?
answer: Yes, I share it so they can help me.

en: We have lived in this house for ten years.
tamil: நாங்க இந்த வீட்டுல பத்து வருஷமா இருக்கோம்.
context: Telling a new neighbour about yourself.
explain: Present perfect with 'for' shows something that started in the past and still continues.
usage: Use it when you talk about how long you have stayed in a place.
leelaQ: How long have you lived in your present house?
answer: We have lived here for five years.

en: Who told you about the accident?
tamil: அந்த விபத்தை பத்தி உங்களுக்கு யாரு சொன்னாங்க?
context: Asking a family member how they heard bad news.
explain: 'Who' asks about the person. After 'who' in a past question, use the past verb directly.
usage: Use it to find out the source of news in a serious situation.
leelaQ: How do you usually get the news every day?
answer: I read it on my phone in the morning.

en: My grandmother used to tell us stories every night.
tamil: எங்க பாட்டி தினமும் ராத்திரி எங்களுக்கு கதை சொல்லுவாங்க.
context: Remembering your childhood with a friend.
explain: 'Used to' shows a regular habit in the past.
usage: Use it to share warm family memories in a chat.
leelaQ: Who told you stories when you were small?
answer: My grandfather told me stories before I slept.

en: How was your journey last night?
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி பயணம் எப்படி இருந்துச்சு?
context: Asking a relative who just arrived.
explain: 'How was...?' asks for an opinion about a past event.
usage: Use it to be polite to guests who travelled a long way.
leelaQ: How was your last long journey?
answer: It was tiring, but the train was on time.

en: I have already finished my report, so I can go home.
tamil: என் ரிப்போர்ட்டை ஏற்கனவே முடிச்சுட்டேன், அதனால நான் வீட்டுக்கு போகலாம்.
context: Telling your team leader you are done.
explain: 'Already' with present perfect shows the work is done earlier than expected.
usage: Use it with a team leader to say your work is completed.
leelaQ: Have you finished all your work for today?
answer: Yes, I have finished everything and I am free now.

en: Can you explain what happened in the meeting yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து மீட்டிங்ல என்ன நடந்துச்சுன்னு விளக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a colleague who attended the meeting.
explain: 'Can you explain' is a friendly request. The next part is in normal statement order.
usage: Use it with a colleague when you missed a meeting.
leelaQ: What did you discuss in your last meeting?
answer: We discussed the plan for next month.

en: The funniest thing happened today; the teacher called me by my father's name.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ஒரு காமெடி நடந்துச்சு, டீச்சர் என்னை எங்கப்பா பேர் சொல்லி கூப்பிட்டாங்க.
context: Telling a friend a funny incident from school or college.
explain: The semicolon joins two related ideas. 'Funniest' is the superlative of 'funny'.
usage: Use it to start a funny story with friends.
leelaQ: What is the funniest thing that happened to you recently?
answer: My friend sat on my chair and fell down laughing.

en: I could not find my keys anywhere this morning.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு காலையில என் சாவியை எங்கயும் காணல.
context: Explaining why you were late.
explain: 'Could not' is the negative past of 'can'. It shows you were not able to do it.
usage: Use it to explain a delay caused by a lost item.
leelaQ: Where do you usually keep your keys?
answer: I keep them on a hook near the door.

en: Early in the morning, we reached Chennai and took a cab to the hotel.
tamil: அதிகாலையில சென்னை போய் சேர்ந்து, கேப் புடிச்சு ஹோட்டலுக்கு போனோம்.
context: Describing the start of a trip.
explain: Time phrases like 'early in the morning' set the scene at the start of a story.
usage: Use it to describe how a journey began.
leelaQ: How did you reach your last holiday place?
answer: We went by train and then took a taxi to the resort.

en: Why were you late to the office yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து ஏன் ஆபீசுக்கு லேட்டா வந்தீங்க?
context: A manager politely asking about a delay.
explain: 'Were' is the past of 'are' for 'you'. 'Why' asks for the reason.
usage: Use it with a team member who came late and needs to explain.
leelaQ: Why were you late the last time?
answer: I was late because of heavy traffic.

en: I slipped on the wet floor, but luckily nobody saw me.
tamil: ஈரத்தரையில வழுக்கி விழுந்துட்டேன், நல்ல வேளையா யாரும் பார்க்கல.
context: Telling a friend about an embarrassing moment.
explain: 'But' shows a good point after a bad event. 'Luckily' adds a positive feeling.
usage: Use it to share an embarrassing but harmless story.
leelaQ: Have you ever felt embarrassed in public?
answer: Yes, I once walked into a glass door in a mall.

en: Have you finished your lunch yet?
tamil: நீங்க இன்னும் லஞ்ச் முடிக்கலையா?
context: Asking a colleague before a meeting.
explain: 'Yet' is used in questions and negatives with present perfect.
usage: Use it to check if someone is free for a meeting.
leelaQ: Have you eaten lunch yet today?
answer: Yes, I have eaten a full meal.

en: Our team has worked on this project since January.
tamil: எங்க டீம் ஜனவரில இருந்து இந்த ப்ராஜெக்ட்ல வேலை செய்யுது.
context: Telling a client how long the project has been going.
explain: 'Since' is used with a starting point in time, like January or Monday.
usage: Use it in meetings to show how long you have been doing something.
leelaQ: Which project have you been working on for a long time?
answer: I have been working on a billing project since March.

en: Please tell us a story from your childhood.
tamil: உங்க சின்ன வயசு கதை ஒண்ணு சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a grandparent or elder.
explain: 'Please' makes it polite. 'From your childhood' says what kind of story.
usage: Use it with elders who enjoy sharing old memories.
leelaQ: Which childhood story do you remember the most?
answer: I remember a story about a clever crow.

en: Last Sunday we cleaned the whole house before the guests came.
tamil: போன ஞாயித்துக்கிழமை விருந்தாளிங்க வர்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி வீடு முழுக்க சுத்தம் பண்ணோம்.
context: Telling a friend how you prepared for guests.
explain: 'Before' joins two past events. The cleaning happened first.
usage: Use it to talk about family chores and preparations.
leelaQ: What did you do last Sunday at home?
answer: I helped my mother clean the kitchen and then we watched TV.

en: The bus did not come on time, so I took an auto.
tamil: பஸ் நேரத்துக்கு வரல, அதனால ஆட்டோ புடிச்சேன்.
context: Explaining a change of plan.
explain: 'Did not come' is negative past. 'So' shows the result.
usage: Use it to explain a small delay to a manager or a friend.
leelaQ: What do you do when the bus does not come?
answer: I take an auto or ask a friend for a lift.

en: I took the wrong train and ended up in a different town.
tamil: தப்பான ரயில்ல ஏறி வேற ஊருக்கு போயிட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a travel mistake.
explain: 'Ended up' means a surprising result at the end of a series of events.
usage: Use it to tell a funny travel mistake story.
leelaQ: Have you ever made a mistake while travelling?
answer: Yes, I once got into the wrong bus and reached another area.

en: What was your favourite game as a child?
tamil: சின்ன வயசுல உங்களுக்கு புடிச்ச விளையாட்டு என்ன?
context: Asking a friend about childhood.
explain: 'Was' is used with 'your favourite game'. 'As a child' talks about the past.
usage: Use it to know more about a new friend or relative.
leelaQ: Which games did you play with friends in childhood?
answer: I loved playing kabaddi with my neighbours.

en: As a child, I was afraid of dogs.
tamil: சின்ன வயசுல எனக்கு நாய்னா பயம்.
context: Talking about your childhood fears.
explain: 'Was afraid of' describes a feeling in the past. Use 'of' after 'afraid'.
usage: Use it to talk about childhood feelings with friends.
leelaQ: What were you afraid of as a child?
answer: I was afraid of the dark and slept with the light on.

en: Did you see the match on TV last night?
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி டிவில மேட்ச் பார்த்தீங்களா?
context: Starting a chat with a friend about cricket.
explain: 'Did you watch' is a simple past question. Add a time like 'last night'.
usage: Use it as a friendly opener the day after a big match.
leelaQ: Which match did you enjoy watching the most?
answer: I enjoyed the World Cup final the most.

en: She has already told me the whole story twice.
tamil: அவ முழு கதையையும் எனக்கு ஏற்கனவே ரெண்டு தடவை சொல்லிட்டா.
context: Politely saying a friend repeats the same story.
explain: 'Twice' shows how many times. Present perfect is used when the time is not important.
usage: Use it gently when someone repeats a story you know.
leelaQ: Do you have a friend who tells the same story again and again?
answer: Yes, my uncle tells the same cricket story every time.

en: Could you repeat what you said about the accident?
tamil: விபத்தை பத்தி நீங்க சொன்னதை திரும்ப சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Politely asking someone to repeat important news.
explain: 'What you said' is a noun clause. It is in normal statement order.
usage: Use it when you did not hear a part of a serious story.
leelaQ: What do you say when you didn't hear someone clearly?
answer: I say, sorry, could you repeat that please?

en: Then the lights went off, and the whole street became dark.
tamil: அப்புறம் லைட் போயிடுச்சு, தெரு முழுக்க இருட்டாயிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a story about a power cut.
explain: 'Then' moves the story to the next event. 'Went off' means stopped working.
usage: Use it to tell a story step by step in an exciting way.
leelaQ: What happened at your home during the last power cut?
answer: We lit candles and talked for an hour.

en: I haven't eaten anything since morning.
tamil: காலையில இருந்து நான் எதுவும் சாப்பிடல.
context: Telling a friend you are very hungry.
explain: 'Haven't eaten' is present perfect negative. 'Since morning' shows the starting time.
usage: Use it with family or friends when you are hungry after a long day.
leelaQ: What do you do when you are very hungry?
answer: I eat something quickly, like biscuits or fruit.

en: We stayed at my uncle's place for two days during the holidays.
tamil: விடுமுறையில ரெண்டு நாள் மாமா வீட்டுல தங்கினோம்.
context: Telling a colleague about your holiday.
explain: 'For two days' shows how long an action lasted in the past.
usage: Use it to say how long you stayed somewhere.
leelaQ: Where did you stay during your last holiday?
answer: We stayed in a small lodge near the beach.

en: How long were you waiting at the bus stop yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து பஸ் ஸ்டாப்ல நீங்க எவ்வளவு நேரம் காத்திருந்தீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a long wait yesterday.
explain: 'How long were you waiting' asks about the length of a past wait.
usage: Use it when a friend was late because of a bus delay.
leelaQ: What do you usually do when you have to wait for a long time?
answer: I listen to songs or talk to people near me.

en: I forgot my lunch box at home, so I bought biryani outside.
tamil: லஞ்ச் பாக்ஸை வீட்டுலயே மறந்துட்டேன், அதனால வெளியில பிரியாணி வாங்கினேன்.
context: Telling a colleague why you ate outside.
explain: 'Forgot' and 'bought' are irregular past forms. 'So' gives the result.
usage: Use it to explain a small change in your plan at work.
leelaQ: What did you have for lunch yesterday?
answer: I had curd rice and potato fry.

en: When did you first come to Chennai?
tamil: நீங்க முதல் தடவை எப்ப சென்னைக்கு வந்தீங்க?
context: Asking a colleague about their background.
explain: 'When did you' asks about a past time. Use the base verb 'come' after 'did'.
usage: Use it to know how long a person has lived in a city.
leelaQ: When did you first come to your current city?
answer: I first came here five years ago for work.

en: I met my school friend by chance at the railway station yesterday.
tamil: நேத்து ரயில்வே ஸ்டேஷன்ல என் ஸ்கூல் ஃப்ரெண்டை தற்செயலா பார்த்தேன்.
context: Telling a family member about a surprise meeting.
explain: 'By chance' means it was not planned. 'Met' is the past of 'meet'.
usage: Use it to share a pleasant surprise with family or colleagues.
leelaQ: Have you met an old friend suddenly somewhere?
answer: Yes, I met my classmate in a supermarket after ten years.

en: Let me finish my story first.
tamil: முதல்ல என் கதையை முடிக்க விடுங்க.
context: Politely stopping an interruption.
explain: 'Let me' asks for permission or space to do something.
usage: Use it politely when someone keeps interrupting you.
leelaQ: What do you do when someone interrupts you?
answer: I politely ask them to let me finish.

en: The train was late, so we reached the function after the muhurtham.
tamil: ரயில் லேட்டா வந்ததால முகூர்த்தம் முடிஞ்சப்புறம்தான் விழாவுக்கு போனோம்.
context: Explaining why you missed part of a wedding.
explain: 'Was late' describes the train. 'So' shows the result of that delay.
usage: Use it to explain to relatives why you came late to an event.
leelaQ: Have you ever reached an event very late?
answer: Yes, I reached a friend's party after the cake cutting.

en: She didn't call me back after the interview.
tamil: இன்டர்வியூக்கு அப்புறம் அவங்க என்னை திரும்ப கூப்பிடல.
context: Telling a friend about a job application.
explain: 'Call back' means to phone again. 'Didn't' is the short form of 'did not'.
usage: Use it to share disappointment about no reply.
leelaQ: What do you do if no one replies to your message?
answer: I wait one day and then call them again.

en: I have learnt to ride a bicycle, and now I ride it daily.
tamil: நான் சைக்கிள் ஓட்ட கத்துக்கிட்டேன், இப்போ தினமும் ஓட்டுறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a new skill.
explain: Present perfect shows a result that matters now. The result here is daily riding.
usage: Use it to talk proudly about a skill you picked up.
leelaQ: What new skill have you learnt recently?
answer: I have learnt to cook rice and sambar.

en: What did your mother say when she saw the marks?
tamil: மார்க்கை பார்த்ததும் உங்க அம்மா என்ன சொன்னாங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a school result story.
explain: 'When' joins two past events in a question.
usage: Use it to ask a friend about their family's reaction.
leelaQ: What did your parents say when you passed an exam?
answer: They were very happy and gave me sweets.

en: My father gave me a watch on my tenth birthday.
tamil: எனக்கு பத்தாவது பிறந்தநாளுக்கு அப்பா ஒரு கடிகாரம் கொடுத்தார்.
context: Sharing a memory about a gift.
explain: 'Gave' is the past of 'give'. 'On my tenth birthday' tells the exact time.
usage: Use it to tell a happy memory about your family.
leelaQ: What was the best gift you got as a child?
answer: I got a new cycle on my birthday.

en: Have you ever missed a flight?
tamil: நீங்க எப்பவாவது ஃபிளைட்டை மிஸ் பண்ணிருக்கீங்களா?
context: Chatting with a friend about travel problems.
explain: Use 'Have you ever' and the past participle 'missed' to ask about a life experience.
usage: Use it to start a talk about travel stories.
leelaQ: Have you ever missed a train or bus? What did you do?
answer: Yes, I missed a train and took the next one.

en: We waited in the queue for two hours, but the counter closed.
tamil: ரெண்டு மணி நேரம் வரிசையில நின்னோம், ஆனா கவுண்ட்டர் மூடிட்டாங்க.
context: Complaining to a friend about a bad experience.
explain: 'But' shows a bad surprise after a long effort.
usage: Use it to tell a frustrating experience at a bank or office.
leelaQ: What do you do when you wait too long in a queue?
answer: I read news on my phone and wait patiently.

en: Please don't stop, tell me the rest of the story.
tamil: நிறுத்தாதீங்க, மீதி கதையை சொல்லுங்க.
context: Encouraging a friend to continue.
explain: 'Don't stop' is a negative imperative. 'The rest' means the remaining part.
usage: Use it while a story is getting interesting.
leelaQ: Do you like listening to stories? Why?
answer: Yes, I like them because they are interesting.

en: The little boy hid behind the door and scared his sister.
tamil: அந்த சின்ன பையன் கதவுக்கு பின்னாடி ஒளிஞ்சுக்கிட்டு தன் தங்கச்சியை பயமுறுத்தினான்.
context: Telling a funny story about children.
explain: 'Hid' is the past of 'hide'. 'Scared' means made someone afraid.
usage: Use it to tell a funny family story about kids.
leelaQ: Did you play tricks on your brother or sister?
answer: Yes, I hid her slippers and she kept searching.

en: We didn't go out yesterday because of the heavy rain.
tamil: பெருமழை காரணமா நேத்து நாங்க வெளியே போகல.
context: Telling a friend why you stayed at home.
explain: 'Didn't go' is the negative past. Use 'because of' with a noun.
usage: Use it to explain why you cancelled a plan.
leelaQ: What do you do at home on a rainy day?
answer: I watch movies and drink hot tea.

en: It was raining heavily, so we stood under a tree for some time.
tamil: பலமா மழை பெய்துக்கிட்டு இருந்துச்சு, அதனால கொஞ்ச நேரம் மரத்துக்கு கீழ நின்னோம்.
context: Describing a rainy day to a friend.
explain: Past continuous (was raining) sets the background of a story.
usage: Use it to describe the weather at the time of an event.
leelaQ: What do you do when it suddenly rains outside?
answer: I stand in a shop and wait till it stops.

en: Did the train leave on time?
tamil: ரயில் சரியான நேரத்துக்கு கிளம்புச்சா?
context: Asking a family member who went to the station.
explain: 'On time' means at the right time. 'Leave' stays in base form after 'did'.
usage: Use it to ask about arrival or departure of any transport.
leelaQ: Does the bus in your area come on time?
answer: No, it is usually ten minutes late.

en: I got my first salary in 2019 and bought a gift for my mother.
tamil: நான் 2019ல முதல் சம்பளம் வாங்கி அம்மாவுக்கு ஒரு பரிசு வாங்கினேன்.
context: Talking about your first job.
explain: Use 'in' with a year. Two past actions are joined with 'and'.
usage: Use it to share a proud memory at work or with family.
leelaQ: What did you do with your first salary?
answer: I gave it to my parents and bought sweets.

en: Where were you born, and where did you grow up?
tamil: நீங்க எங்க பிறந்தீங்க, எங்க வளர்ந்தீங்க?
context: Getting to know a new colleague.
explain: 'Were you born' uses 'be' in the past. 'Did you grow up' uses 'did' plus a base verb.
usage: Use it politely to learn about someone's hometown.
leelaQ: Where were you born and where did you grow up?
answer: I was born in Trichy and grew up in Chennai.

en: She has changed her job twice since she moved to Bangalore.
tamil: அவ பெங்களூர் போனதுல இருந்து ரெண்டு தடவை வேலை மாத்தியிருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend about a relative's career.
explain: 'Since' plus a past event shows the starting point of the time period.
usage: Use it to give news about someone's life.
leelaQ: Has any of your friends moved to another city?
answer: Yes, my friend has moved to Hyderabad for work.

en: Can you share your trip photos with me?
tamil: உங்க டிரிப் போட்டோக்களை எனக்கு ஷேர் பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend after a group trip.
explain: 'Share with me' means send to me. 'Can you' is a casual request.
usage: Use it after a trip or a function to ask for pictures.
leelaQ: Do you take many photos on your trips?
answer: Yes, I take lots of photos of places and food.

en: The teacher scolded the whole class because somebody broke the window.
tamil: யாரோ ஜன்னலை உடைச்சதால டீச்சர் முழு கிளாஸையும் திட்டினாங்க.
context: Remembering a school incident.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason for something that happened.
usage: Use it to tell school stories to friends or children.
leelaQ: Do you remember any funny moment from school?
answer: Yes, our teacher fell asleep in the class once.

en: I have never been so embarrassed in my life.
tamil: என் வாழ்க்கையில இவ்ளோ அவமானப்பட்டதே இல்ல.
context: Telling a friend about a very awkward moment.
explain: 'Have never been' talks about the whole life up to now.
usage: Use it to describe a really awkward moment you went through.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about an embarrassing moment?
answer: I once called my teacher 'mom' in front of the class.

en: I woke up late, had a quick bath, and ran to the bus stop.
tamil: லேட்டா எந்திரிச்சேன், அவசரமா குளிச்சுட்டு பஸ் ஸ்டாப்புக்கு ஓடினேன்.
context: Describing a rushed morning.
explain: Several past actions in a row are separated with commas and 'and'.
usage: Use it to describe your morning to a friend or colleague.
leelaQ: How was your morning today?
answer: I woke up early, did yoga, and had breakfast.

en: What was the funniest thing that happened in your school?
tamil: உங்க ஸ்கூல்ல நடந்த காமெடியான விஷயம் என்ன?
context: Asking a friend for a funny story.
explain: 'The funniest thing that happened' uses the superlative and past tense together.
usage: Use it to start a fun chat with friends.
leelaQ: Can you share a funny incident from your school days?
answer: Our teacher once came to class with two different shoes.

en: My neighbour has helped us a lot since we moved here.
tamil: நாங்க இங்க வந்ததுல இருந்து எங்க பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரர் நிறைய உதவி பண்ணியிருக்கார்.
context: Thanking or praising a neighbour to others.
explain: Present perfect shows help that started in the past and still matters.
usage: Use it to speak kindly about someone who supported you.
leelaQ: Who has helped you the most in your life?
answer: My elder sister has helped me a lot in my studies.

en: And then what happened?
tamil: அப்புறம் என்ன ஆச்சு?
context: Encouraging a friend to continue a story.
explain: A short question that shows you are interested in the story.
usage: Use it while someone is telling you a story to keep them going.
leelaQ: When your friend tells a story, what do you ask?
answer: I ask, then what happened?

en: When the bell rang, all the children ran out of the class.
tamil: மணி அடிச்சதும் எல்லா குழந்தைகளும் கிளாஸை விட்டு ஓடினாங்க.
context: Describing a school scene.
explain: 'When' joins two events that happened one after another.
usage: Use it to describe a scene or event in a story.
leelaQ: What did you do when the school bell rang?
answer: I ran to the ground to play with my friends.

en: Tell me exactly what you saw at the shop.
tamil: கடையில நீங்க என்ன பார்த்தீங்கன்னு சரியா சொல்லுங்க.
context: A shop owner or a family member asking for details.
explain: 'Exactly' asks for clear details. 'Saw' is the past of 'see'.
usage: Use it when you want the facts, for example after a complaint.
leelaQ: What do you notice when you enter a new shop?
answer: I notice the prices and the number of customers.

en: I didn't know the answer, but I smiled and tried anyway.
tamil: எனக்கு பதில் தெரியல, ஆனா சிரிச்சுக்கிட்டே முயற்சி பண்ணினேன்.
context: Telling about an interview or exam moment.
explain: Negative past uses 'did not' plus the base verb: 'did not know'.
usage: Use it to tell how you handled a hard situation.
leelaQ: How did you feel in your last interview or exam?
answer: I felt nervous at first, but I answered calmly.

en: They did not inform me that the meeting was cancelled.
tamil: மீட்டிங் கேன்சல் ஆனதை அவங்க எனக்கு சொல்லவே இல்ல.
context: Complaining politely at work.
explain: 'Did not inform' is a negative past. It is a polite way to complain.
usage: Use it politely when you were not told about a change.
leelaQ: How do you want to be told about a change in plan?
answer: I would like a message or a call in advance.

en: Last night we ate dinner on the terrace because of the heat.
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி வெக்கை தாங்காம மொட்டை மாடியில சாப்பிட்டோம்.
context: Telling a friend about a summer night.
explain: 'Because of' is followed by a noun like 'the heat'. 'Ate' is the past of 'eat'.
usage: Use it to describe a small family moment.
leelaQ: What did you do last night after dinner?
answer: We sat outside and talked for a while.

en: Have you heard what happened at the party last night?
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி பார்ட்டில என்ன நடந்துச்சுன்னு கேள்விப்பட்டீங்களா?
context: Sharing gossip with a friend.
explain: 'Have you heard' starts news. 'What happened' is the news itself.
usage: Use it to start sharing news or a surprising story.
leelaQ: Have you heard any interesting news today?
answer: Yes, I heard that our road will be repaired.

en: We have already booked the tickets for the temple trip.
tamil: கோவில் பயணத்துக்கு டிக்கெட் ஏற்கனவே புக் பண்ணிட்டோம்.
context: Telling a family member the plan is ready.
explain: Present perfect with 'already' shows an action is complete before now.
usage: Use it to tell relatives that arrangements are done.
leelaQ: Have you planned anything for the next holiday?
answer: Yes, we have planned a trip to Kerala.

en: How did you reach the airport so early?
tamil: நீங்க எப்படி இவ்ளோ சீக்கிரம் ஏர்போர்ட்டுக்கு வந்தீங்க?
context: Asking a friend with surprise.
explain: 'How did you' asks about the way something was done.
usage: Use it when you are surprised someone came earlier than expected.
leelaQ: How did you reach your office today?
answer: I came by metro and then walked.

en: I danced on the stage for the first time, and my legs were shaking.
tamil: நான் முதல் தடவை மேடையில டான்ஸ் ஆடினேன், கால் நடுங்கிக்கிட்டு இருந்துச்சு.
context: Telling a friend about a first-time experience.
explain: 'For the first time' is used to talk about something new in your life.
usage: Use it to share a nervous but memorable moment.
leelaQ: What was the first time you spoke or performed in front of people?
answer: I gave a speech in school and I was very nervous.

en: Could you describe how the accident happened?
tamil: விபத்து எப்படி நடந்துச்சுன்னு விவரிக்க முடியுமா?
context: A police officer or an insurance person asking.
explain: 'Describe how' asks for a clear explanation in steps.
usage: Use it in formal situations like an insurance call or a police station.
leelaQ: Can you describe your house in a few words?
answer: It is a small house with two rooms and a garden.

en: Two days ago, a cow stood in the middle of the road for ten minutes.
tamil: ரெண்டு நாள் முன்னாடி ஒரு மாடு பத்து நிமிஷம் ரோட்டு நடுவுல நின்னுச்சு.
context: Telling a friend why you were stuck in traffic.
explain: 'Ago' goes after the time: 'two days ago'. It always shows past time.
usage: Use it to explain a traffic delay or a funny road scene.
leelaQ: What was the strangest thing you saw on the road?
answer: I saw a dog riding on a scooter with its owner.

en: I lived in Coimbatore until I finished my school.
tamil: நான் ஸ்கூல் முடிக்கிற வரைக்கும் கோயம்புத்தூர்ல இருந்தேன்.
context: Introducing your background to a new colleague.
explain: 'Until' shows the time when something stopped.
usage: Use it when you talk about where you grew up.
leelaQ: Where did you live before you came here?
answer: I lived in a small village near Erode.

en: Did you remember to lock the door before leaving?
tamil: போகும் முன்னாடி கதவை பூட்டுறது ஞாபகம் இருந்துச்சா?
context: Asking a family member after leaving home.
explain: 'Remember to' is for a task you needed to do. Use it for reminders.
usage: Use it with family members after you leave the house.
leelaQ: Do you always check the door and windows before going out?
answer: Yes, I check them twice before I leave.

en: The shopkeeper gave me extra change by mistake, so I returned it.
tamil: கடைக்காரர் தப்பா அதிகமா சில்லறை கொடுத்துட்டார், நான் திருப்பிக் கொடுத்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about an honest moment.
explain: 'By mistake' means not on purpose. 'Returned' means gave it back.
usage: Use it to tell a short story about honesty.
leelaQ: Have you ever found something that was not yours?
answer: Yes, I found a purse and gave it to the police.

en: What did you eat for dinner yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து நைட் டின்னருக்கு என்ன சாப்பிட்டீங்க?
context: Making small talk with a friend.
explain: 'Eat' stays in base form after 'did'. The answer will use 'ate'.
usage: Use it for easy small talk about daily life.
leelaQ: What was your dinner last night, and who cooked it?
answer: I ate dosa and chutney at home.

en: We all laughed so much that the teacher sent us out.
tamil: நாங்க எல்லாரும் ரொம்ப சிரிச்சதால டீச்சர் வெளியில அனுப்பிட்டாங்க.
context: Telling a funny school memory.
explain: 'So much that' joins a strong action with its result.
usage: Use it to tell a funny memory from school or college.
leelaQ: Did you ever get sent out of the class?
answer: Yes, once I was talking to my friend in class.

en: Please start from the beginning.
tamil: தயவு செய்து ஆரம்பத்துல இருந்து சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking someone to explain a story in order.
explain: 'From the beginning' means from the first part. It helps you follow the order of events.
usage: Use it when you did not understand a long story or problem.
leelaQ: How do you explain a problem to someone clearly?
answer: I start with the first step and go in order.

en: I have been to Delhi only once, and it was very cold.
tamil: நான் டெல்லிக்கு ஒரே ஒரு தடவை தான் போயிருக்கேன், ரொம்ப குளிரா இருந்துச்சு.
context: Telling a colleague about your travel experience.
explain: 'Have been to' means you went and came back. It talks about experience.
usage: Use it to say what places you have visited in life.
leelaQ: Which cities have you visited so far?
answer: I have visited Chennai, Madurai and Bangalore.

en: Her phone rang in the middle of the meeting, and everybody looked at her.
tamil: மீட்டிங் நடுவுல அவ ஃபோன் அடிச்சுது, எல்லாரும் அவளை பார்த்தாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about an embarrassing office moment.
explain: 'In the middle of' means during. 'Rang' is the past of 'ring'.
usage: Use it to tell a short office incident to friends.
leelaQ: What should we do with our phone during a meeting?
answer: We should keep it silent or on vibration.

en: Have you told your parents about the new job yet?
tamil: புது வேலையை பத்தி அப்பா அம்மாகிட்ட சொல்லிட்டீங்களா?
context: Asking a friend about family news.
explain: 'Told' is the past participle of 'tell'. 'Yet' asks if it is done by now.
usage: Use it to ask a friend if they shared important news.
leelaQ: Who was the first person you told about your good news?
answer: I first told my mother.

en: Last year I fell sick before my exam, but I still passed.
tamil: போன வருஷம் பரீட்சைக்கு முன்னாடி உடம்பு சரியில்லாம போச்சு, ஆனாலும் பாஸ் பண்ணிட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a hard time.
explain: 'Fell sick' means became ill. 'Still' shows a surprising result.
usage: Use it to share how you handled a difficult time.
leelaQ: Did you ever work hard in spite of a problem?
answer: Yes, I studied for my exam even with a fever.

en: Which school did you go to as a child?
tamil: சின்ன வயசுல நீங்க எந்த ஸ்கூலுக்கு போனீங்க?
context: Asking a new friend about their education.
explain: 'Which' asks to choose from a group. 'Did you go' is a past question.
usage: Use it when you meet someone new and talk about the past.
leelaQ: What was your school like when you were a child?
answer: I went to a government school near my house.

en: I saw an old photo of my school yesterday, and I felt so happy.
tamil: நேத்து என் ஸ்கூலோட பழைய போட்டோவை பார்த்தேன், ரொம்ப சந்தோஷமா இருந்துச்சு.
context: Sharing a nice memory with a friend.
explain: 'Saw' is the past of 'see'. 'Felt' tells the feeling after the event.
usage: Use it to talk about nostalgia with friends and family.
leelaQ: What old memory makes you happy?
answer: My school trip to Kanyakumari always makes me happy.

en: Can you tell me what you did after you left the office?
tamil: ஆபீஸை விட்டு கிளம்பினதுக்கு அப்புறம் என்ன பண்ணுனீங்கன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend about their evening.
explain: Two past verbs 'did' and 'left' show the order of events.
usage: Use it to ask someone about their day in a friendly way.
leelaQ: What do you do after you leave the office?
answer: I go home, rest, and then cook dinner.

en: Please wait, I will tell you the full story.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் இருங்க, நான் முழு கதையையும் சொல்றேன்.
context: Asking a friend to be patient.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise. 'Please wait' politely asks for time.
usage: Use it when a story is too long to tell quickly.
leelaQ: What do you say when you need a little time to explain?
answer: I say, please wait, I will explain it clearly.

en: Just tell me what the doctor said yesterday.
tamil: நேத்து டாக்டர் என்ன சொன்னார்னு மட்டும் சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a relative who visited a doctor.
explain: 'Just' makes the request short and direct. 'Said' is past tense.
usage: Use it with family when you are worried and want a quick answer.
leelaQ: Do you visit the doctor often?
answer: No, I visit only when I am really sick.
